text.en: Find the notes of line 1: each one waits until you're on it.

text.en: In Sephardic and British synagogues the whole congregation sings it at the close of the Sabbath and festival morning services, and it is chanted almost everywhere on the eve of Yom Kippur.

source.en: The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 1 (Funk and Wagnalls, 1901), p. 205, "Adon 'Olam", read from the archive.org text

text.en: Record the tune of Adon Olam in Sing, with the other parts playing.
Its last lines, "into His hand I commit my spirit when I sleep and when I wake", led the scholar Seligman Baer to think it was first meant to be said before going to sleep.

source.en: The Jewish Encyclopedia, vol. 1 (Funk and Wagnalls, 1901), p. 206, "Adon 'Olam", citing Baer's prayer-book commentary (Rödelheim, 1868), read from the archive.org text
